name: McLaren
bio: Founded by Bruce McLaren, the Woking squad is one of the sport's great dynasties. Back-to-back constructors' crowns in 2024 and 2025 capped a remarkable rebuild, and Lando Norris delivered the drivers' title in 2025.

name: Mercedes
bio: The Silver Arrows defined the V6 turbo-hybrid era with eight straight constructors' titles from 2014 to 2021. The 2026 power-unit rules give Brackley a fresh shot at the front.

name: Red Bull Racing
bio: From energy-drink upstart to six-time champions. 2026 is a new chapter: Red Bull builds its own power unit for the first time, in partnership with Ford.

name: Ferrari
bio: The only team to have raced in every season of the world championship, and the most successful constructor in history. Leclerc and Hamilton form one of the most star-studded line-ups on the grid.

name: Williams
bio: Frank Williams' team won nine constructors' titles between 1980 and 1997. Under James Vowles, and with Sainz and Albon, the Grove outfit is climbing back up the order.

name: Racing Bulls
bio: Red Bull's second team, formerly Minardi, Toro Rosso and AlphaTauri. It is the proving ground for young talent — Vettel, Verstappen and Gasly all won here or passed through.

name: Aston Martin
bio: Lawrence Stroll's ambitious project pairs a new Silverstone campus with legendary designer Adrian Newey and works Honda power for 2026.

name: Haas
bio: The first American team of the modern era, run lean with close technical ties to Ferrari. Ocon and Bearman lead its midfield charge.

name: Audi
bio: Audi takes over the former Sauber team for 2026 and becomes a full works entry, building its own power unit in Neuburg, Germany.

name: Alpine
bio: The Enstone factory won titles as Benetton and Renault. For 2026 Alpine ends its own engine program and switches to Mercedes power.

name: Cadillac
bio: The grid's 11th team and the first new entry since 2016. Backed by General Motors, Cadillac arrives with veterans Pérez and Bottas and Ferrari power.
